architectures_ok: Dev board plus breakout modules hand-wired (soldered hook-up wire or Dupont jumpers) inside a printed or cut case, e.g. Raspberry Pi Pico/Pico W or an ESP32 board + MH-Z19C or SCD41 breakout + 0.96 in SSD1306 OLED + WS2812B stick (the research's low reference build).

Dev board and modules plugged into a custom 2-layer carrier PCB through headers/sockets (Curious Electric: NodeMCU on the Cheese Board carrier; AirGradient DIY Basic/Pro: D1 Mini on an AirGradient PCB).
Perfboard or stripboard carrier instead of a fabricated PCB.
Solderless plug-together chain: dev board + STEMMA QT / Qwiic / Grove CO2 sensor, display and LED modules.

Dev board with a built-in screen (Adafruit ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT Feather, Waveshare ESP32-S3 1.47 in, Waveshare RP2350-LCD-0.96 or similar) + CO2 sensor on a cable in a separate pod or compartment + a separate RGB LED, or the board's onboard RGB LED exposed through a window or light pipe (KnowCO2 layout with a real light added).

Fully custom PCB with MCU, regulator, USB-C (with CC pull-downs) and LEDs as SMD, with the sensor as a module on headers or a reflowed bare SCD4x (Watterott CO2-Ampel, AirGradient ONE style), provided the quote covers fabrication and assembly.

Sensor powered from raw USB 5 V (5 V NDIR such as MH-Z19C or S8; the SCD4x (2.4-5.5 V) and SCD30 (3.3-5.5 V) also run from 5 V) or from 3.3 V (SCD4x; an SCD30 at its 3.3 V minimum with a flag-and-measure note) via the dev board's or breakout's regulator, or from a dedicated LDO/boost.

Light as addressable RGB (WS2812B/SK6812, single pixel, stick, ring or jewel) with correct level handling, a discrete RGB or red/green bicolour LED on GPIO/PWM with resistors, or red/amber/green LEDs behind one diffuser; one LED or a light bar.

Enclosure as an FDM-printed case, a laser-cut plate sandwich on standoffs with open sides and a frosted front as diffuser (Curious Electric), an off-the-shelf vented box such as Hammond 1551V translucent with cut-outs (Watterott), or a main case plus separate sensor pod (KnowCO2).
A bought enclosure (a Hammond box, a dev kit's own housing or similar) counts if the CAD models the cut-outs, vents and sensor placement that the mechanical traps check.
Firmware in any language and toolchain: CircuitPython, MicroPython, Arduino C++, ESP-IDF or ESPHome; Wi-Fi on or off.
Power from a USB wall adapter or a computer port, through micro-USB or USB-C.

roles.role: CO2 sensor (true CO2, NDIR or photoacoustic NDIR)
roles.accepts: Any sensor that measures CO2 directly: Sensirion SCD40/SCD41 (bare LGA on a custom PCB with reflow/PCBA, or a breakout such as Adafruit 5190/5187, Pimoroni, Seeed Grove, M5Stack, DFRobot SEN0536), Sensirion SCD30, Senseair S8 LP / S88, Winsen MH-Z19C/MH-Z19E/MH-Z16, Infineon PAS CO2 (supply per the chosen variant's datasheet; a 12 V emitter rail needs a boost converter and a line in the current budget). MH-Z19B and MH-Z14A are marked discontinued by Winsen: accept only with a named in-stock source. A refurbished or B-Ware sensor counts if quotes.json flags it and the build plan makes outdoor calibration mandatory. Does NOT count: eCO2/VOC estimators (CCS811, SGP30, SGP40/41, ENS160, BME680/688).
roles.why: The product is a CO2 monitor; MOX eCO2 parts infer CO2 from VOCs and are not CO2 sensors. All four real monitors use NDIR: MH-Z14A (Curious Electric), SCD41 (KnowCO2), SCD30/SCD4x (Watterott), Senseair S8 (AirGradient).

roles.accepts: Any MCU that can read the sensor's interface (I2C or UART) and drive the screen and the light: RP2040/RP2350 boards (Pico, Pico W, Pico 2), ESP32 / ESP32-C3 / ESP32-S3 boards, ESP8266 (NodeMCU, D1 Mini), SAMD21, an AVR Arduino (with level handling for 3.3 V parts), or an MCU on a custom PCB. A dev board with a built-in screen covers this role and the screen role at once. Wi-Fi is not needed.
roles.why: Something must read the sensor, apply thresholds and drive the display and light. Real monitors use ESP8266 (Curious Electric), ESP32-S3 (KnowCO2), SAMD21 (Watterott), ESP32-C3 (AirGradient ONE).

roles.role: Small screen showing the CO2 value
roles.accepts: A display that shows the current reading in ppm as digits, readable at desk distance: 0.91-1.5 in I2C/SPI OLED (SSD1306, SH1106), 1-2 in TFT/IPS (ST7789, ILI9341), small e-paper (e.g. 1.54 in) refreshed within its maker's limits (Waveshare: full refresh no more often than every 180 s; partial refresh only on panels that support it, with a periodic full refresh; at least one refresh per 24 h, https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/1.54inch_e-Paper_Module_Manual), 16x2 character LCD, or a dev board's built-in display. A 4-digit 7-segment display that shows the ppm number is acceptable at the low end. An LED bar graph or the coloured light alone does not count.
roles.why: The idea asks for a small screen. Real monitors use a 0.96 in SSD1306 OLED (Curious Electric), 1.14 in ST7789 TFT (KnowCO2), 1.3 in SH1106 OLED (AirGradient).

roles.accepts: A light source separate from the screen's pixels that can show at least green and red (a yellow/amber middle or continuous blend is expected): addressable RGB LED(s) (WS2812B/SK6812/NeoPixel single pixel, stick, ring or jewel) with correct data level handling, a discrete RGB LED or red/green bicolour LED driven by GPIO/PWM through resistors or a transistor, red/amber/green discrete LEDs behind one diffuser, or a dev board's onboard RGB LED if the case exposes it through a window or light pipe. Not enough on its own: colouring the number on the screen (KnowCO2 does this, but the idea names a screen and a light as two things), or a single-colour LED.
roles.qty: 1 or more LEDs, seen as one light
roles.why: The idea's light is the at-a-glance signal. Real monitors: 5x WS2812B under a frosted plate (Curious Electric), 4x WS2812B in a translucent box (Watterott), 11-LED WS2812B bar shining through the case (AirGradient).

roles.accepts: A USB receptacle reachable from outside the closed case that powers the whole device from 5 V: the dev board's own micro-USB or USB-C, or a USB-C receptacle on a custom carrier with separate 5.1 kOhm Rd on CC1 and CC2, or a micro-USB/USB-C breakout (a USB-C breakout must have the Rd resistors). Power-only or power+data both count.
roles.why: The idea says powered by USB. Every real monitor uses USB (micro-USB on Curious Electric, USB-C on KnowCO2, Watterott and AirGradient).

roles.accepts: A USB cable as a bom.json line whose device end matches the receptacle (USB-A to micro-B, USB-A to C, or C-to-C only when the device has Rd on CC), data-capable if it is also used to flash firmware, about 1-2 m for a desk. The line may be bought, or marked 'owned / not purchased' if it names both connectors and 'data-capable'; owned lines are exempt from the URL, price and stock checks. A wall adapter is not required (see not_required) unless the current budget exceeds what a computer port gives.
roles.why: The idea needs a USB power path; Curious Electric lists the lead only as an 'Additional Item Required', and KnowCO2 notes the cable must carry data for flashing.

roles.accepts: Whatever makes the electrical connections, documented as a netlist (cad/pcb.mjs) or a wiring table with pin names: custom carrier PCB with headers, perfboard/stripboard, soldered hook-up wire, Dupont jumpers, or STEMMA QT / Qwiic / Grove cables. Every connection to sensor, screen and light (power, ground, data, pull-ups) must be listed.
roles.why: Any architecture needs its connections defined before logic levels, rails and current can be checked.

roles.role: Enclosure with airflow to the sensor
roles.accepts: Any housing that protects the electronics, fixes the parts and lets room air reach the sensor: FDM-printed case (PLA/PETG), laser-cut acrylic or plywood plates on standoffs with open sides (Curious Electric), an off-the-shelf vented box such as Hammond 1551V (translucent version doubles as diffuser, Watterott), or a main case plus separate sensor pod (KnowCO2). It must have vents at the sensor's inlet, a screen window, a light aperture or diffuser and a USB opening. A bought housing (a Hammond box, a dev kit's own case) counts if the CAD models its cut-outs, vents and sensor placement. A bare board with no case does not count.
roles.qty: 1 (may be several printed or cut parts)
roles.why: A desk product needs a case; CO2 reaches NDIR sensors only by diffusion, so vents at the sensor are functional, not cosmetic.

roles.accepts: Means to hold each board, the sensor and the screen in fixed positions, and to make the unit stand on a desk with screen and light facing the user: screws, heat-set inserts or standoffs through PCB holes, printed clips, rails or bosses (KnowCO2's sensor bay and slide-in body; AirGradient's case holds the PCB with no screws), snap-fit lids, plus a flat base, wedge, feet or stand (Curious Electric trapezoid plates stand upright). The sensor must be held by its PCB or pins, never by its optical body; adhesive only away from the sensor.
roles.qty: as needed (typically 4-8 fasteners or printed clips)
roles.why: Loose parts move, stress the sensor and misalign windows; the idea is a desk device so it must stand on its own.

roles.accepts: Optional. If present, budget its TX current (ESP32-S3 355 mA) and keep the radio module away from the sensor.
roles.why: The idea asks for a local screen and light only; Wi-Fi is an extra the real monitors have.

roles.accepts: Optional. If a button shares a boot-strap pin, note the boot behaviour (Curious Electric's GPIO15 button stops boot if held).
roles.why: Not in the idea; thresholds can be compile-time constants.

roles.accepts: Optional; if used, a transistor driver and a mute or delay (Watterott users found buzzers a nuisance).
Optional. The idea says powered by USB.
Optional (SCD4x/SCD30 give T/RH for free; SHT4x module). If shown, a temperature offset must be set (trap sensor-away-from-heat).
Optional; required only if the current budget exceeds 500 mA. Must be an EU-plug 5 V supply rated at least the budget.
roles.why: Users usually own a USB charger; KnowCO2's US-plug adapter shows the trap of listing the wrong one.

traps.requirement: Keep the CO2 sensor's supply pin inside its datasheet range while it draws its peak current on real USB power. The source must be able to deliver that peak at the rail voltage used. Datasheet values: MH-Z19C and MH-Z14A 5.0 +/-0.1 V nominal, 4.5-5.5 V allowed (manual note 9.6), supply able to give at least 150 mA, peak 125 mA; Senseair S8 LP 4.5-5.25 V, 300 mA peak (ESPEasy warns 5.2 V or more can damage the lamp); SCD4x 2.4-5.5 V, peak 205 mA at 3.3 V or 137 mA at 5 V, ripple 30 mV p-p or less, LDO recommended; SCD30 3.3-5.5 V, 75 mA max, so 5 V is the safer rail and a nominal 3.3 V rail sits at its minimum. A 5 V-only NDIR part goes on raw VBUS or a regulated 5 V; if it sits behind a Schottky, PTC or dev-board diode, the drop is computed at peak current and must keep the pin at 4.5 V or above. Local decoupling at the sensor is expected. Bulk capacitance above ~10 uF directly on VBUS goes behind a regulator or soft-start, or is noted.
traps.why: USB VBUS is 4.75-5.50 V at the connector under the USB 2.0 VBUS ECN, and the USB external-circuit guidance limits VBUS bulk capacitance to about 10 uF (Renesas). A 1N5819 drops up to ~0.6 V at 1 A and a 500 mA PTC (MF-R050) is 0.41-1.17 ohm, so the Curious Electric kit's sensor rail can sit around 4.4-4.7 V (research estimate), at or below the MH-Z14A's 4.5 V minimum; NodeMCU VIN is itself fed through an on-board diode. AirGradient users measured 4.61-4.82 V at the board from a 5.24 V supply over ordinary micro-USB cables, close to the S8's 4.5 V floor; that thread's dropouts were finally traced to read timing and a bad Rx joint, and AirGradient staff still advise a stable supply. AirGradient's DIY Pro added optional 2x 470 uF for weak supplies. The SCD4x needs a quiet supply (Adafruit: '~200mA peak'), and the Adafruit SCD-4x breakout's own regulator is rated only 'at least 100mA'. Watterott's reference design runs its SCD30 from its 3.3 V LDO with 4.7 uF plus 100 nF on 3V3. A design that just wires sensor VCC to a '5V' pin looks right and fails on a long cable or a laptop port.
traps.pass_if: Take the sensor's supply range and peak current from design.json/bom.json, and from cad/pcb.mjs nets (or the wiring table) the net on the sensor's VDD pin plus every series element between it and the USB connector. PASS if all hold: (1) the rail is named and its worst-case voltage (stated, or 4.75 V minus listed series drops for VBUS-derived rails, or the regulator's nominal output) is inside the sensor's datasheet range: 4.5-5.5 V for MH-Z19C, MH-Z19B and MH-Z14A, 4.5-5.25 V for the S8, 2.4-5.5 V for the SCD4x, 3.3-5.5 V for the SCD30. At a range edge or outside a tighter nominal (an MH-Z19C on raw VBUS, outside 5.0 +/-0.1 V; an S8 on raw VBUS, whose maximum can exceed 5.25 V; an SCD30 on a nominal 3.3 V rail), design.json or build-plan.md must flag it and tell the builder to measure the sensor pins under load; with that note an MH-Z19C on a Pico's VBUS pin passes. (2) The source's current rating is at least the sensor's peak at the rail voltage used plus the other loads on that rail (an SCD4x powered at 3.3 V from a regulator rated 100 mA fails). (3) For a bare SCD4x or S8 on a custom PCB, or sensor leads longer than about 20 cm (grading allowance), bom.json or the netlist has a local capacitor at the sensor supply (at least 4.7 uF plus 100 nF, the Watterott reference design; grading allowance); for a breakout or module on short leads this is advisory, and the module's own capacitors or regulator count. (4) The capacitance the design adds directly on VBUS is 10 uF or less, or the excess sits behind a regulator or soft-start, or design.json notes the deviation. FAIL if the rail is unstated; the worst-case rail is outside the sensor's datasheet range; an edge case named in (1) has no flag-and-measure note; the source is rated below the sensor's peak; or a 5 V-only sensor sits behind a Schottky, PTC or board diode with no computed drop.

traps.requirement: Every signal between the MCU and the sensor and screen must be within both ends' logic levels at the rails actually used. With a 3.3 V MCU whose pins are not 5 V tolerant (ESP32-S3 max input VDD+0.3 V; check the chosen MCU's datasheet) no SDA/SCL/RX may be pulled or driven to 5 V: power I2C OLED modules from 3V3, or confirm that their pull-ups go to the module's own 3.3 V regulator, since some expose 5 V pull-ups on the header when fed 5 V. A bare SCD4x powered at 5 V needs VIH = 0.65 x 5 = 3.25 V, so run it at 3.3 V, level-shift, or use a breakout whose documented logic-level setting gives at least that. The SCD30's I2C lines have internal 45 kOhm pull-ups to 3 V and a VIH of 1.75-3.0 V: pull-ups to 3.3 V are accepted (the Watterott Pro runs its SCD30 bus at 3.3 V), pull-ups to 5 V are not, and its SEL pin must stay at 4.0 V or below. With a 5 V MCU (Uno/Nano), the S8's RX (3.3 V logic, absolute maximum about 3.8 V) needs a divider or shifter. MH-Z19/MH-Z14 UARTs are 3.3 V with 5 V compatibility. Exceeding a pin's absolute maximum (5 V into the S8 RxD) can damage it outright.
traps.why: These faults often work on the bench and then fail intermittently or stress pins. AirGradient's early boards mixed 5 V and 3.3 V I2C (the maker called it 'not compliant'), measured 1.1 Vpp ripple and slow edges, and moved everything to one level. The Curious Electric kit relies on the MH-Z14A UART being '3.3 V (5V compatible)' to wire it straight to the ESP8266.
traps.pass_if: In cad/pcb.mjs or the wiring table (design.json/build-plan.md), list each MCU-sensor and MCU-display net with the supply voltage of each end and where its pull-ups connect; cited pull-up and module documentation (schematic, listing or guide) counts as evidence. PASS if, for every net, the driver's high level is at least the receiver's VIH and no more than the receiver's maximum input: all I2C pull-ups go to 3V3 with a 3.3 V MCU; the OLED is powered from 3V3, or the module's schematic/listing shows its I2C pull-ups go to its own 3.3 V regulator output, or its 5 V pull-ups are recorded as removed or shifted; an SCD4x powered at 5 V sees an I2C high level of at least 3.25 V through a shifter or a documented logic-level jumper setting; an SCD30 bus is pulled up to 3.3 V or less and its SEL pin stays at 4.0 V or below; any 5 V-powered I2C/UART part talking to a 3.3 V MCU has a shifter or divider; and checks.json or design.json records the check. FAIL if any 3.3 V MCU pin sits on a net pulled or driven to 5 V (unless the MCU datasheet, cited, rates that pin 5 V tolerant under the operating conditions), or the sensor's or display's supply is unstated.

traps.requirement: If the light is a WS2812B/SK6812-class addressable LED powered from 5 V and the MCU is 3.3 V, the data input must meet the LED's VIH. Accepted fixes: a buffer powered from the LED supply whose own input threshold (VIH or VT+ max) at that supply is at or below the GPIO high level (74AHCT125 or 74HCT245 per Adafruit; 74LVC1G17, VT+ max 2.79 V at 5.5 V, as Curious Electric does), or a dual-supply translator powered at 3.3 V and 5 V; a series diode lowering the LED supply so that 0.7 x VLED is at or below the GPIO high level (Watterott's BAS3010); or an LED part whose datasheet VIH fits (WS2812B-V5 VIH 2.7 V at 5 V). The GPIO high level is the output at DIN's sub-mA load: take 3.3 V for a 3.3 V IO rail. An external addressable LED must never run below its datasheet minimum VDD (WS2812B 3.5 V absolute, WS2812B-V5 and SK6812mini 3.7 V). A 300-500 ohm resistor in the data line near the first LED is recommended. Discrete RGB or bicolour LEDs need a series resistor per channel and must stay within the GPIO current rating, or use a transistor driver.
traps.why: Older WS2812B VIH is 0.7 x VDD = 3.5 V at 5 V, above any 3.3 V GPIO. Adafruit: with a 3.3 V microcontroller 'you must use a logic level shifter' such as a 74AHCT125 or 74HCT245, or run the pixels near logic voltage. The plausible design wires a NeoPixel stick's DIN straight to a Pico or ESP32 pin with VDD on 5 V. It usually lights on the bench but can flicker or show wrong colours, which defeats the one job of the light. A buffer whose own VIH is 0.7 x VCC at 5 V fails the same way, so the buffer's threshold is checked too. The ESP32-S3's VOH min of 0.8 x VDD = 2.64 V is a loaded-output figure; DIN draws almost no current, so the pin sits close to its 3.3 V rail, which is why the Watterott diode fix and the WS2812B-V5 work. Feather-class boards power their on-board NeoPixel from 3.3 V, so on-board LEDs are exempt.
traps.pass_if: Find the light in bom.json and its supply and data nets in cad/pcb.mjs or the wiring table. PASS if any one holds: (a) a buffer or level-shifter IC powered from the LED supply sits between the GPIO and DIN, and its datasheet VIH (or VT+ max) at that supply is at or below the GPIO high level (e.g. 74AHCT125, 74HCT245, 74LVC1G17), or it is a dual-supply translator powered at 3.3 V and 5 V; (b) the LED VDD is fed through one or more diodes, and design.json shows 0.7 x VLED (VLED = 5.0 V minus the diode's Vf at the LED current, from the cited diode datasheet) at or below the GPIO high level (3.3 V for a 3.3 V IO rail), stating the margin and that VLED stays above the LED's minimum VDD; (c) the LED part's datasheet VIH at the VDD used is at or below the GPIO high level (3.3 V for a 3.3 V IO rail), with the datasheet cited; (d) the light is the dev board's own on-board RGB LED; (e) it is a non-addressable LED with a resistor per channel and per-channel current within the MCU pin rating, or driven by a transistor. FAIL if a 5 V-powered WS2812B/SK6812 has its DIN wired straight to a 3.3 V GPIO without (a)-(c), or if an external addressable LED runs below its datasheet minimum VDD (WS2812B 3.5 V absolute, WS2812B-V5 and SK6812mini 3.7 V). A dev board's on-board LED is exempt under (d).

traps.requirement: The design must add up the worst-case coincident current of every load: sensor peak (at the rail voltage used: SCD4x 205 mA at 3.3 V, 137 mA at 5 V), MCU (including Wi-Fi TX if the radio is on), display, LEDs at the firmware's brightness, and regulator losses. The total must fit the USB source: 500 mA for a USB 2.0 port or a Type-C Default source, unless a supply of 1 A or more is specified (and, with the design's own USB-C sink, detected through CC). Mitigations: cap LED brightness and light only the R/G channels, keep Wi-Fi off or limit its TX power, use fewer LEDs.
traps.why: ESP32-S3 TX alone is 355 mA, SCD41 peaks at 205 mA at 3.3 V, one WS2812B draws up to 60 mA at full white (so an 8-pixel stick at white is about 480 mA), and an OLED about 20 mA. ESP32-S3 + SCD41 + 1 LED + OLED comes to about 640 mA (research estimate), over 500 mA. AirGradient documents that under-rated adapters cause a distorted display, sensor dropouts and random restarts. The Curious Electric kit's worst case (~0.6 A, estimate) is above its 500 mA PTC's hold current (MF-R050 class: hold 0.5 A, trip 1.0 A), so it may trip when warm.
traps.pass_if: PASS if design.json, checks.json or build-plan.md has a current-budget table giving each load's average and peak and a summed coincident peak, and either (i) the summed peak, computed under limits the firmware actually enforces (an LED brightness/channel cap constant, Wi-Fi off or TX power set), is 500 mA or less, or (ii) bom.json includes a 5 V supply rated at least the summed peak and build-plan.md says to use it. The sensor's peak may be taken at the rail voltage actually used. FAIL if there is no budget, the budget relies on limits the firmware does not set, or the sum exceeds the stated source.

traps.requirement: If the design has its own USB-C receptacle (on a custom carrier PCB, or a bought USB-C breakout that is not part of a dev board), CC1 and CC2 must each have their own 5.1 kOhm pull-down (Rd) to GND. A single shared resistor or floating CC pins is wrong.
traps.why: A USB-C source turns VBUS on only when it sees Rd. With only VBUS and GND wired, a C-to-C cable or a USB-C charger supplies no power, so the device works only with A-to-C cables. Watterott (R3/R4 5.1 kOhm) and AirGradient DIY Pro (2x 5.1 kOhm 'for smart adapters') fit them. A plausible board wires VBUS, GND, D+ and D- and forgets CC.
traps.pass_if: If bom.json or cad/pcb.mjs contains a USB-C receptacle or USB-C breakout that is not part of a dev board: PASS only if the netlist shows two separate 5.1 kOhm resistors, CC1 to GND and CC2 to GND, or the breakout's datasheet or listing is cited as having them. If power enters through a dev board's own USB connector or through micro-USB, PASS as not applicable, recorded as N/A in checks.json.

traps.requirement: Room air must reach the sensor's inlet through openings next to it, with little dead volume, and nothing may press on the sensing body. The inlet is the membrane on top of the SCD4x cap, the SCD30's cavity (open top and bottom), the S8's particle filter, or the MH-Z diffusion window. For an S8, leave at least 1.5 mm between the particle filter and the cover and at least 1.0 mm from the optical bench (Senseair ANO102); give an SCD30 at least 1 mm standoff above the host PCB (Sensirion). Other sensors have no maker minimum: keep the inlet uncovered and case features about 1 mm clear of the sensing body (grading allowance for print tolerance). Hold the sensor by its PCB or pins only. Put it in its own compartment or pod, or face its inlet out through a cut-out or open side as Curious Electric does, so it samples room air rather than air trapped in the case.
traps.why: Sensirion: put a large opening close to the sensor, keep dead volume small, and isolate it from air trapped in the housing; for the SCD30, 'the larger the opening, the better the air exchange'. Senseair: do not block the particle filter and apply no force to the OBA. Winsen: no pressure on the gilded chamber from any direction, and good ventilation at the diffusion window. A closed printed box with a vent grid on the far side looks plausible but gives slow, damped readings; a lid rib on the can shifts the reading.
traps.pass_if: In cad/*.py (with system.json placement), locate the sensor's inlet face and the enclosure wall or opening in front of it. PASS if: (1) vent openings in that wall, or an open side or cut-out, overlap or adjoin the inlet's projection; (2) if a wall or lid lies in front of the inlet, the inlet is not covered and, for an S8, the filter-to-cover gap is at least 1.5 mm (Senseair ANO102); an inlet at an open side or inside a cut-out meets (2); (3) no case feature comes within 1 mm of the sensor's cap, chamber or optical bench (Senseair's OBA minimum and Sensirion's SCD30 standoff; a grading allowance for other sensors), and the sensor is held by screws, standoffs, headers or clips on its PCB; (4) an internal wall, a separate pod or an outward-facing cut-out separates the sensor's air from the electronics' air, or design.json states the small inner volume around the sensor. system.json gap and contact probes that check these count. FAIL if the nearest vents do not face the inlet, the inlet is covered, or a rib, lid or clamp touches the sensing body.

traps.requirement: Place the CO2 sensor away from the significant heat sources, and preferably below them: a Wi-Fi/BLE module or SoC with its radio on, a linear regulator dissipating more than about 0.1 W ((Vin - Vout) x I), a backlit TFT/LCD, and LEDs drawing more than about 20 mA in total (both thresholds are grading allowances). With a dev board that has a built-in screen, put the sensor off the board (pod, cable, or far end of the case), not on its back. If the device shows temperature or humidity, the firmware must set a temperature offset.
traps.why: Sensirion names the CPU, display, Wi-Fi module and regulators as heat sources and says to place the sensor at maximal distance, in the lowest and coolest part, because hot air rises; a PCB slit decouples it. The SCD30 drifts +/-2.5 ppm/degC, and thermal stress on a transmissive NDIR chamber 'can significantly falsify CO2 readings'. Watterott's Plus put the Wi-Fi module under the SCD30 and needed a larger temperature offset than the Pro (issue #44); Watterott's firmware uses +8 degC on Wi-Fi boards against +4 degC without Wi-Fi. The Pro's SCD30 sits about 33 mm centre-to-centre in x from the LDO (about 12 mm edge-to-edge, a reviewer's calculation from the board file). KnowCO2 moved its SCD41 into a separate pod 'to reduce self-heating'. Curious Electric's sensor sits in a gap of roughly 10 mm (estimate from its 10 mm spacers) behind the carrier that holds the ESP8266, with open sides but no thermal barrier (instructions PDF steps 12-14). A low-power MCU without a radio dissipates little, so it is not treated like a Wi-Fi SoC.
traps.pass_if: Using system.json positions (or cad/*.py placement), list the significant heat sources: any Wi-Fi/BLE module or SoC with the radio enabled, linear regulators dissipating more than ~0.1 W ((Vin - Vout) x I), a backlit TFT/LCD, and LEDs above ~20 mA total. PASS if the sensor is not directly above any of them, and is either at least 10 mm edge-to-edge from each (grading allowance) or separated by an internal wall, a separate pod, or a PCB slot/cable. If design.json lists a temperature or humidity readout, the firmware sets a temperature offset or build-plan.md has a step to tune it. FAIL if the sensor is stacked on or over an active radio module or regulator, or mounted on the back of a built-in-screen dev board.

traps.requirement: With the case closed and the unit on a desk: the screen's active area must be fully visible through a window on the side facing the user. The light must be visible from the front through an aperture, light pipe or translucent/frosted diffuser, not hidden behind the screen module or an opaque wall. The USB connector must be reachable through a cut-out sized for the cable's plug: the plug shell when the receptacle face sits flush with the outer surface, the plug overmould when the receptacle is recessed behind it; and the board must be fixed so plugging in does not load the connector's solder joints. The unit must stand stably with screen and light facing the user.
traps.why: Each real monitor solves this explicitly. Curious Electric uses a frosted front with an OLED window and a glowing top edge; Watterott a translucent Hammond box 'ideal for applications where LEDs should be visable' [sic]; AirGradient LEDs that shine through the plastic. KnowCO2's assembly check is that the USB-C port aligns with its side cut-out, and AirGradient ships a 90-degree USB-C cable so the ONE can sit flush against a wall. A CAD case can hold every part yet size the window to the module outline, hide the LED or wall off the port, and then the product fails the idea outright.
traps.pass_if: From cad/*.py and system.json, PASS if all four hold: (1) a window in the front face covers the display's active area (taken from the display's datasheet or model dimensions), and the display faces front; (2) a straight line from the LED to the outside, on the front or top, passes through an opening, a light pipe or a part named as translucent or diffuser material in design.json, with no opaque part in between; (3) a cut-out in line with the USB receptacle with its axis clear: if the receptacle face is within about 0.5 mm of the outer surface (grading allowance), the opening clears the plug shell plus ~0.5 mm per side (about 9.5 x 3.5 mm for USB-C, 8.5 x 3.5 mm for micro-B; estimate); if it is recessed deeper, the opening clears the plug overmould at full insertion (about 12.5 x 7 mm for USB-C; estimate, no plug drawing cited; larger for 90-degree plugs, advisory); (4) the base gives a stable desk stance with the front toward the user, shown by a system.json stability probe or a stated tilt or stand. FAIL if any of the four is missing.

traps.requirement: Only if the sensor is an SCD30 on I2C: every bus that carries it must run at 100 kHz or less (Sensirion recommends 50 kHz or lower), the MCU's I2C implementation must support clock stretching, and the read path must tolerate stretches of up to 150 ms (a driver timeout of at least 150 ms, or retries). Using the SCD30's Modbus/UART mode instead is also fine. Not applicable to any other sensor.
traps.why: Sensirion's SCD30 interface description: 'Maximal I2C speed is 100 kHz', 50 kHz or lower recommended; the master must support clock stretching, which is typically 30 ms and can reach 150 ms once per day. A plausible design shares the bus with an OLED at 400 kHz, or uses an I2C driver with a short clock-stretch timeout, and then fails intermittently.
traps.pass_if: If bom.json names an SCD30 wired for I2C: PASS if the frequency of the SCD30's bus (as set in the firmware, or the I2C stack's default if none is set, stated in design.json) is 100 kHz or less, and either the I2C timeout is at least 150 ms (set in firmware or stated in design.json) or the read path retries on a failed read; or the SCD30 is wired in Modbus/UART mode with SEL at 4.0 V or below. If the sensor is not an SCD30, PASS as N/A, recorded in checks.json. FAIL if the SCD30's bus is set above 100 kHz (for example shared with a display at 400 kHz), the bus frequency is neither set nor stated, or neither an I2C timeout of at least 150 ms nor a retry on a failed read is shown.

traps.requirement: The colour bands must be numeric ppm thresholds in the firmware with a cited basis. They must be monotonic, with green ending between 800 and 1000 ppm, full red starting between 1000 and 2000 ppm, adjacent edges at least 100 ppm apart (comparable to the sensors' +/-60-100 ppm accuracy at 1000 ppm), and hysteresis or averaging so the colour does not flap at an edge. A yellow/amber middle band or a continuous blend is expected; a blend runs from pure green at a sourced value of 1000 ppm or less to pure red at a sourced value between 1000 and 2000 ppm, with the hue monotonic in between.
traps.why: Credible bases: UBA/AIR (under 1000 harmless, 1000-2000 ventilate, over 2000 unacceptable); REHVA's epidemic-time guidance (amber 800, red 1000); Italy's ISS (1000 ppmv as a first management value); Eurovent 2024 (under 900 / 900-1200 / over 1200). Real monitors: Watterott's default is green from 600, yellow at 1000 and red at 1200, with blue below 600 (its COVID profile is 600/800/1000/1200/1400); KnowCO2 800/1200 with an alert at 1500; AirGradient green up to 800, yellow up to 1000, orange up to 1500, red up to 2000. Accuracy near 1000 ppm is +/-75 (SCD41), +/-100 (SCD40, MH-Z19C), +/-70 (S8) and +/-60 (SCD30) ppm, so 50 ppm bands are noise. Watterott users asked for hysteresis because the alert flapped (issue #18), and Watterott colours on an averaged reading.
traps.pass_if: In the firmware (e.g. code.py constants), find the ppm band edges (or the blend's end points) and the code that maps a reading to a colour. PASS if all hold: the thresholds are integer ppm constants; design.json or build-plan.md names their source (UBA/AIR, REHVA, ISS, EN 16798-1, Eurovent, or a cited real monitor); for bands, green's upper edge is between 800 and 1000, the edge where the light becomes fully red is between 1000 and 2000, and the edges increase monotonically with adjacent edges at least 100 ppm apart; for a continuous blend, pure green ends at or below a sourced value of 1000 ppm or less, pure red starts at a sourced value between 1000 and 2000 ppm, and the hue is monotonic in between (no edge-spacing rule); and the firmware applies hysteresis (different rising and falling edges) or averages readings (moving average or EMA) before choosing a colour. FAIL if the thresholds are missing, unsourced or non-monotonic, or green can persist above 1000 ppm.

traps.requirement: The firmware must set the sensor's automatic self-calibration (ASC/ABC) state explicitly for desk use, or design.json must name the datasheet default and say why it suits a desk unit; and the build plan must give a correct manual calibration procedure. ASC/ABC assumes regular fresh air and continuous power: SCD4x needs at least 3 min near 400 ppm per week and runs of at least 4 h (on by default); MH-Z19/MH-Z14 use 24 h cycles from power-on (on by default); SCD30 needs 7 days with 1 h of fresh air daily (off by default); S8 runs about 180 h per period. A unit on a laptop port that powers off nightly, or in a room that never airs out, drifts low and shows green when the air is bad. SCD4x configuration commands work only while idle, so stop periodic measurement before setting ASC, altitude or offset, then restart it. Those settings are volatile unless persisted, and persist_settings writes an EEPROM rated for at least 2000 write cycles, so it must not run on every boot. On MH-Z19/MH-Z14 the HD pin must be unconnected, tied high or driven high from reset, because holding it low for 7 s or more triggers a zero calibration.
traps.why: KnowCO2's driver sends ASC and altitude after starting periodic measurement, which Sensirion lists as not executable, and its error wrapper swallows the failure, so the settings are likely ignored; the Adafruit CircuitPython driver's force_calibration also leaves the sensor stopped. Watterott's calibration accepts any stable 200-800 ppm reading and forces it to 400, so an indoor 'calibration' reads low by the indoor excess (derived); one user reported ~220 ppm indoors and 0 outdoors after calibrating (issue #1, cause unconfirmed). AirGradient users saw errors of hundreds of ppm from ABC false baselines, and the S8's fixed 400 ppm target sits below today's ~429 ppm outdoor air (NOAA global mean 428.73 ppm in May 2026, as quoted by AirGradient).
traps.pass_if: PASS if all hold: (1) the firmware issues an explicit ASC/ABC enable or disable for the chosen sensor at boot (e.g. SCD4x set_automatic_self_calibration_enabled, the SCD30 ASC command, MH-Z19 ABC on/off, the S8 ABC period register), and for an SCD4x this happens after stop_periodic_measurement and before start_periodic_measurement; or design.json names the sensor's datasheet default ASC state and says why it suits a desk unit; (2) build-plan.md has a manual calibration step: outdoors or at an open window, away from people and traffic, for at least the sensor's minimum (SCD4x more than 3 min running; SCD30 at least 2 min in continuous mode; MH-Z19C/E at least 20 min at about 400 ppm (its manual also says 30 min; either passes) then HD low for 7 s or more, or the UART zero-point command where the manual documents one; MH-Z14A at least 20 min then HD low for 7 s or more; S8 at least 15 min then bCAL held 4-8 s or its background-calibration command), against 400 ppm where the sensor's target is fixed, otherwise the current outdoor background (400-440 ppm) with its source, and with a warning not to calibrate indoors; (3) build-plan.md or design.json says what ASC needs (continuous power, regular fresh air) and that a sleeping computer port defeats it; (4) for MH-Z19/MH-Z14, HD is unconnected, tied high, or on a GPIO the firmware drives high from reset and whose reset state does not hold it low for 7 s or more; (5) the firmware does not call persist_settings, or any equivalent sensor EEPROM write, on every boot (writing once when a value changes is fine). FAIL if the ASC state is neither set nor documented, calibration is not described, or settings are persisted on every boot.

traps.requirement: From power-on until the sensor's preheat has passed and a first valid reading arrives, the light must not show steady green and the screen must say it is warming up. Preheat per datasheet: MH-Z19B 3 min; MH-Z14A 1 min (manual V1.4 and product page; the older manual's 3 min is accepted as conservative); MH-Z19C 1 min; S8 LP under 60 s; the SCD4x gives its first reading after one 5 s interval in standard periodic mode (discard the first single-shot reading after a wake-up); the SCD30 boots in under 2 s. If the sensor stops answering, or returns an out-of-range or stale value (no new reading for more than about 3 measurement intervals, a grading allowance: 15 s at the SCD4x's 5 s interval, 90 s in its 30 s low-power mode), the light must leave steady green and the screen must show an error.
traps.why: A dead or warming sensor that leaves the light green gives false reassurance. Watterott made the LEDs turn red on a CO2-sensor error only in firmware v20. KnowCO2 shows '!! SENSOR ERR' after 30 s without data. AirGradient marks values outside 0-10000 as invalid (-1), and its users saw -1/-2/-3 readings. Curious Electric's firmware has a 'Warm Up Sensor' stage; its instructions list a menu item '10: Adjust Warm Up time', 'Recommended > 180s' (instructions PDF p.11 as read by the research; a reviewer could not re-check it because that page is an image). A fixed 30 s timeout would falsely fault an SCD4x in low-power periodic mode (one reading per 30 s) or single-shot mode.
traps.pass_if: In the firmware, PASS if both exist: (1) a warm-up state lasting at least the chosen sensor's preheat (a constant, or until the first valid reading for sensors with no preheat), during which the light is anything except steady green (off, blue, white, amber or blinking) and the display shows a warming-up message; (2) a fault path that, on a read failure, CRC error, timeout, value outside the sensor's range, or no new reading for more than about 3 of the configured measurement intervals (grading allowance), sets the light to something other than steady green (off, blinking or red) and shows an error. An emulator run or a checks.json case with the sensor missing is extra evidence. FAIL if the colour logic runs on a default initial value (e.g. 0 or 400 ppm shown as green) before the first valid reading.

traps.requirement: Every purchased part must come from a shop that ships to Italy from the EU (or the line must carry EU import VAT and duty), with a product URL, price and checked stock. Lines marked 'owned / not purchased' (a USB cable or filament the user already has) need no URL, price or stock but must name the item exactly. The CO2 sensor must be a true NDIR or photoacoustic part that is in stock; a discontinued part (MH-Z19B, MH-Z14A) needs a named in-stock source. A refurbished or B-Ware sensor is acceptable only if quotes.json flags it and build-plan.md makes the outdoor calibration mandatory. Parts should be consolidated into a few shops, because each extra shop adds about EUR 6-25 of shipping.
traps.why: EU sources exist for this exact product: Reichelt IT (MH-Z19C EUR 32.29, Pico EUR 4.92, 0.96 in OLED EUR 7.17, NeoPixel stick EUR 2.82, all including 22% IVA; also a Seeed Grove SCD41 at EUR 42.44 and a bare SCD41-D-R2 at EUR 38.91), Berrybase (Adafruit SCD-41 EUR 52.90, Reverse TFT Feather EUR 24.90), Mouser IT (bare SCD41 EUR 22.84 gross, S8 LP EUR 39.88 gross, a research price not re-checked by the reviewers), Futura Elettronica (SCD41 EUR 39.00; its listing does not say whether it is a breakout). Several cheaper listings are out of stock (Berrybase's new MH-Z19C, Pimoroni SCD41), while Berrybase sells an in-stock 'B-Ware' MH-Z19C at EUR 16.40 that a cost-optimising pipeline may pick. Winsen marks the MH-Z19B and MH-Z14A discontinued. Buying from Adafruit US, Tindie or a UK shop adds import VAT and courier fees.
traps.pass_if: In quotes.json and bom.json, PASS if all hold: each purchased line has seller, URL, unit price, currency, stock status and a ship-to-Italy note (lines marked 'owned / not purchased' are exempt but must name the item); every seller is EU-based (e.g. Reichelt, Berrybase, TME, Mouser IT, Futura Elettronica, Eckstein, Opencircuit, Kiwi, RS Italy) or the non-EU line carries import VAT and duty; the sensor line is a true NDIR or photoacoustic CO2 sensor (e.g. SCD30, SCD4x, S8/S88, MH-Z19C/E, MH-Z16, PAS CO2; a discontinued MH-Z19B/MH-Z14A only with a named in-stock source), in stock, and not an eCO2 part (CCS811, SGP30, SGP4x, ENS160, BME68x); a refurbished or B-Ware sensor is flagged in quotes.json and build-plan.md makes outdoor calibration mandatory; a USB cable line exists (bought, or owned naming both connectors and 'data-capable'); and the order uses 3 shops or fewer, or the extra shipping is justified. FAIL if any purchased line lacks a URL or stock status, the sensor is out of stock or discontinued with no named in-stock source, a B-Ware sensor is unflagged, or the sensor is an eCO2 part.

traps.requirement: The quote must be the landed cost of one unit in Italy. It must include VAT (22% IVA, or the VAT the shop states it charges), shipping to Italy for each shop, and any below-threshold shipping charge (Mouser IT ships free only above EUR 75). Non-EU fab or print services (JLCPCB, JLC3DP) must carry IOSS VAT plus the EU EUR 3 duty per goods category on parcels under EUR 150 (from 1 Jul 2026); Italy's extra EUR 2 fee is expected only from 1 Dec 2026, and an EU handling fee on small distance-sale parcels was agreed on 26 Mar 2026 with its amount and start date still pending. A bare SMD sensor must carry its PCB and assembly costs.
traps.why: Shipping is a large share of a ~EUR 60 build: Reichelt EUR 9.95, Berrybase EUR 9.90, TME about EUR 5.98 gross; Mouser IT is free above EUR 75 and charges shipping below that (EUR 25 reported for Mouser.de, unconfirmed for Italy). Mouser shows net prices, so a quote that sums net part prices comes out EUR 15-30 under the real cost (estimate). A bare SCD4x looks cheap (EUR 22.84 gross) but needs reflow or PCBA and, ordered alone, pays Mouser's below-EUR 75 shipping. Sound all-EU builds below EUR 60 exist: about EUR 44-47 landed from Berrybase with its B-Ware MH-Z19C (EUR 16.40), or about EUR 53 once its new MH-Z19C (EUR 25.90) is back in stock (reviewer estimates), so a low total alone is not a failure.
traps.pass_if: In quotes.json, PASS if all hold: there is one shipping line per shop with its amount to Italy; prices are marked gross or VAT is added (22% unless the shop's stated VAT applies); non-EU fab or print lines include VAT and the EUR 3 duty per goods category; a custom PCB with SMD parts includes assembly, or the plan says it is hand-assembled and lists the parts; lines marked 'owned / not purchased' are left out of the total; and the grand total is between EUR 60 and EUR 175 (costBandEur), or the deviation is explained. A total under EUR 60 passes when every line is itemised with shipping and VAT and any refurbished/B-Ware part is flagged. FAIL if a shipping, VAT or duty line is missing, a non-EU line lacks VAT/duty, the sensor is an eCO2 part, or the total is under about EUR 40 without a line-by-line justification in quotes.json or design.json.

traps.requirement: build-plan.md must take a builder from parts to a verified unit. It must cover: flashing the firmware (the exact method for the board, with a data-capable cable); checking the rails before fitting the sensor; bench-testing the display, light and sensor; a breath/response test; an outdoor calibration; safe sensor handling (fitted last, no touching the membrane or chamber, no IPA or flux cleaning, glue or coating near it); closing the case; and placement (away from the user's breath, heat and sun, powered continuously).
traps.why: Sensirion's SCD4x handling notes forbid solvents (IPA, ethanol, acetone) and coatings, ask that the sensor go in after other materials cure, and warn that minor cuts to the membrane cause irreversible damage. Senseair says never to touch the S8 bare-handed or put force on the OBA. Sensirion's design-in test: after 15 min of equilibration, readings should step by 20 ppm or less, and a rise of 1000 ppm or more should show a response in under 60 s. Shipping shock shifts sensor baselines (Checkmk saw 530 and 370 ppm floors), so recalibrate after assembly. KnowCO2 needs a data-capable cable for flashing. ISS: the measurement point and the instrument can shift readings by up to 250 ppm.
traps.pass_if: PASS if build-plan.md contains all of: (1) a flashing step naming the method (e.g. UF2/BOOTSEL then CircuitPython plus copying code.py and its libraries, or an Arduino/esptool upload) and a data-capable cable; (2) a power check: the unloaded rails measured before the sensor is connected, and the sensor supply measured at its pins under load after it is fitted and before the case is closed (expected value from sensor-rail-in-range-at-peak); (3) a functional test, after flashing, in which the screen shows ppm, breathing near the vents raises the reading by hundreds of ppm within about 60 s, the light goes from green to red (by breath or a test mode), and the reading then recovers; (4) a calibration step or explicit ASC instructions consistent with the firmware (calibration-and-asc), done after final assembly; (5) sensor-handling cautions (fit it last; no solvents, flux cleaning, glue, tape or coating on or near it; hold it by the PCB edges) at or before the step that fits the sensor; (6) final placement and continuous-power advice. Only the orderings named here are enforced. FAIL if flashing, testing or calibration is missing.

costBandEur.basis: Delivered to Italy, one unit, VAT included. Prices fetched 2026-10-19 (research, re-checked by a reviewer the same day); conversions use ECB rates of 16 Oct 2026 (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html). LOW (EUR 60) is the cheapest all-new, in-stock, single-shop EU build, all from Reichelt IT at 22% IVA: MH-Z19C EUR 32.29, Raspberry Pi Pico EUR 4.92, 0.96 in SSD1306 OLED EUR 7.17, 8x WS2812 stick EUR 2.82, 40 F/F jumper wires EUR 1.64 (https://www.reichelt.com/it/it/shop/product/developer_boards_-_jumper_cable_40_poles_f_f_20_cm-282700; a reviewer could not find this set on 2026-10-19, so treat it as ~EUR 1.5, estimate) and micro-USB cable EUR 1.84 (https://www.reichelt.com/it/it/shop/product/usb_2_0_a_plug_to_micro-usb_b-plug_1m-74221; a reviewer found one at EUR 1.38, https://www.reichelt.com/it/it/shop/search/micro%20usb%20cavo%201m) make EUR 50.68; DHL to Italy adds EUR 9.95 for EUR 60.63. About 60 g of PLA (~EUR 0.71, estimate) and 4 screws (~EUR 0.20) bring it to about EUR 61.5 with a home-printed case (printer assumed owned). Level handling for the stick and capacitors add about EUR 1-2 (estimate); a print service instead of a home printer adds EUR 15-30 (estimate), giving EUR 75-90. Cheaper sound builds exist: about EUR 44-47 landed from Berrybase alone with its in-stock B-Ware MH-Z19C (EUR 16.40), Pico EUR 4.10, Grove 0.96 in OLED EUR 5.60, WS2812 stick EUR 2.60, about EUR 4 of cables, EUR 9.90 shipping and about EUR 1 of 19%->22% VAT adjustment, or about EUR 53 once its new MH-Z19C (EUR 25.90) is back in stock (reviewer estimates; https://www.berrybase.de/en/search?search=co2+sensor). So EUR 40-60 is acceptable when every line is itemised with shipping and VAT and any B-Ware part is flagged; under about EUR 40 almost certainly omits shipping or VAT or uses an eCO2 sensor. HIGH (EUR 175) is a comfortable KnowCO2-style build from Berrybase: Reverse TFT Feather EUR 24.90, Adafruit SCD-41 EUR 52.90, Qwiic cable EUR 2.30 (shown unavailable at Berrybase; Eckstein's STEMMA QT cable is EUR 2.25, https://eckstein-shop.de/Concepts-Qwiic-Cable-EN__Tier1_1), NeoPixel Jewel EUR 6.90 (the in-stock RGBW SK6812 variant), USB-C cable EUR 2.90 and screws make EUR 90.14, plus EUR 9.90 shipping and about EUR 2.27 Italian VAT adjustment (EUR 102.31). A service-printed case (EUR 10-35) and standoffs bring it to about EUR 115-140. design: design.json names a true CO2 sensor and gives its supply range, peak current at the rail voltage used, interface, preheat time, default ASC/ABC behaviour and accuracy near 1000 ppm.

Every rail (VBUS, 5 V, 3V3) is stated along with the parts on it, including the worst-case voltage at the sensor pins after series diodes, PTC and cable; the sensor's rail is inside its datasheet range (SCD4x 2.4-5.5 V and SCD30 3.3-5.5 V, so 5 V suits both), with a flag-and-measure note at a range edge.
A netlist (cad/pcb.mjs) or wiring table covers the sensor, screen and light with pin names and pull-up locations, and logic levels are checked net by net (including WS2812B DIN level handling).

A current budget lists average and peak per load and compares the sum with the USB source (500 mA unless a larger supply is specified), with firmware brightness and Wi-Fi limits matching the assumptions.
The USB connector is chosen; an own USB-C receptacle has separate 5.1 kOhm Rd on CC1 and CC2.

Enclosure CAD (cad/*.py) has openings facing the sensor inlet; a sensor compartment, pod, outward-facing cut-out or stated small inner volume; the sensor away from, and preferably below, the significant heat sources (radio module, regulator, backlight, LEDs); a screen window over the active area; a light aperture or diffuser; a USB cut-out sized for the plug; and a stable desk stance; system.json gates check these.

Colour thresholds (or blend end points) are in ppm with a cited source (UBA/AIR, REHVA, ISS, Eurovent or a real monitor), with hysteresis or averaging; warm-up and sensor-fault states are defined; the ASC choice and calibration plan are stated; an SCD30 on I2C runs at 100 kHz or less.

Any reuse of open designs respects their licences: the KnowCO2 hardware is CERN-OHL-S (keep the notice and Source Location on the product or its documentation); AirGradient and Watterott are CC BY-SA (attribution, share-alike); nothing is copied from Curious Electric, which has no licence.
source: Every purchased line is from an EU shop that ships to Italy (e.g. Reichelt IT, Berrybase, TME, Mouser IT, Futura Elettronica, Opencircuit, Kiwi, RS Italy), or is non-EU with import VAT and duty shown, with URL, price, VAT basis and stock checked on the quote date; items the user already has are marked 'owned / not purchased'.

The sensor is NDIR or photoacoustic (e.g. SCD4x, SCD30, S8, MH-Z19C/E, MH-Z16, PAS CO2), in stock; a discontinued part only with a named in-stock source; a refurbished or B-Ware part flagged; never an eCO2 part.

The BOM includes the USB cable (bought or owned), the wiring or carrier, fasteners and standoffs, case material or print service, any level shifter and capacitors, and a PCB fab line if a custom board is used.
Shops are consolidated (about 1-3); the quote shows per-shop shipping to Italy, the Mouser shipping charge if under EUR 75, and IOSS VAT plus the EUR 3 per-goods-category duty for JLCPCB/JLC3DP.
The total landed cost falls within EUR 60-175, or the deviation is explained (an itemised build down to about EUR 40 can be sound).
build: Flash the firmware with the board-specific method (e.g. BOOTSEL + UF2 + CircuitPython libraries, or Arduino/esptool upload) using a data-capable cable.
Before fitting the sensor, power up and measure the unloaded rails; after fitting it and before closing the case, measure the sensor supply at its pins under load.
Bench test: the screen shows ppm, the light cycles green to amber to red in a test mode or with breath, the sensor answers, and the fault state triggers when the sensor is unplugged.
Breath/response test: reading rises by hundreds of ppm within about 60 s and recovers; after about 15 min of equilibration, readings are steady.

Calibrate outdoors or at an open window for the sensor's minimum time, against 400 ppm where the sensor's target is fixed, otherwise the current outdoor background (400-440 ppm, with its source), never indoors; do it after final assembly; state the ASC setting and that the unit should stay powered continuously.
Handle the sensor by its PCB edges, fit it last, and keep solvents, flux cleaning, glue, tape and coatings away from it; use no clamping on the optical body.
Close the case and check the screen window, the light visibility and USB access; place the unit on the desk away from the user's breath, heat sources and direct sun.

not_required: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cloud upload, MQTT, Adafruit IO, Home Assistant, a web setup portal or OTA updates (all four real monitors have some of these).
Buttons, a rotary encoder, menus, or on-device threshold editing; compile-time thresholds are fine.
A buzzer or audible alarm (Watterott).
A battery, LiPo charger, fuel gauge or low-power mode (KnowCO2).
A temperature/humidity readout (SHT4x, or the SCD4x/SCD30 T/RH outputs); a temperature offset is needed only if T/RH is shown.
A barometric pressure sensor or automatic pressure compensation (Watterott Pro); an altitude setting is a nice-to-have, not required.
PM2.5, TVOC or NOx sensors (AirGradient ONE).
An ambient light sensor, auto-dimming or a night schedule.
Graphs, min/max, trend arrows, CO2 integral, data logging, or USB serial/JSON output.
An external hardware watchdog (AirGradient's TPL5010); firmware fault handling is enough.
A power switch, a second power input (screw terminal) or ORing diodes (Curious Electric).
Wall-mount keyholes or junction-box mounting holes.
A USB wall adapter in the BOM, unless the current budget exceeds 500 mA.
An ESD array and PTC on the USB input when power comes through a dev board (recommended only for a custom USB-C board).
A colour-blind palette.
A multi-LED light bar; one RGB LED behind a diffuser is enough.
A large or colour display; a 0.96 in monochrome OLED is enough.
CE/RoHS marking, OSHWA certification, or factory calibration certificates and serial logging.
Antenna keep-outs (only relevant if Wi-Fi is used).
Buying a USB cable: an owned cable listed in bom.json as 'owned / not purchased', naming both connectors and 'data-capable', is enough.

An I2C rise-time or bus-capacitance calculation. Advisory when the sensor sits in a pod on a cable longer than about 30 cm (grading allowance): AirGradient users measured ~700 ns rise time with 10 kOhm pull-ups, 'only marginal for 100 kHz', and duplicate pull-up sets caused instability (https://forum.airgradient.com/t/i2c-investigation-of-airgradient-pcbs/640); KnowCO2's pod uses a short STEMMA QT cable (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/knowco2-project/knowco2-hardware/main/bom/bom.csv).

OLED burn-in mitigation (dimming, a screen saver or pixel shift). Advisory only: a Midas OLED spec gives 20,000 h to 50% luminance (about 2.3 years always on, derived) and advises against showing fixed information for long (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/3120883.pdf).
